newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Strong debut seen for Glorious Sun.
newsitem.headline: Strong debut seen for Glorious Sun.

text.p: Causal wear maker and retailer Glorious Sun Enterprise Ltd is expected to post a solid listing debut on Tuesday, analysts said on Friday.
Analysts said Glorious Sun's debut should be strong in light of the company's promising earnings outlook and overwhelming 236 times subscription of its flotation.
"Its earnings growth is seen promising in the coming one to two years in view of its retail expansion in China," said Bonnie Lai, analyst from Yamaichi International.
"As the markets in Australia and New Zealand are already established, earnings contribution growth will be mainly from expansion of its retail business in China," Lai said.
"Its debut should be strong," said Carol Lai, research manager from Amsteel Securities. "Investors like the stock because of its China retail play concept."
She also said the stock would gain support from fund managers switching from H-shares to red-chips and China concept stocks.
H-shares are stocks of China-incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong.
"Outlook for this sector (China retail market) is positive as market is talking about the positive impact to the China economy on the relaxation of austerity measures," Lai said.
Analysts said the grey market price for Glorious Sun was at about HK$2.10 per share as on Friday.
"The shares are expected to trade above HK$2.0 and it has room to edge up towards HK$2.60," one analyst said.
Analysts said the stock would be valued between HK$2.40 to HK$2.60 based on their forecast earnings ratio of 12 to 14 times for whole of 1997.
"We consider the stock will be fairly valued at price of HK$2.45 and we still expect there is more upside potential in long run," said Kathleen Emerson, analyst at DBS Securities.
Glorious Sun has offered a total 250 million new shares, comprising a retail offer of 100 million and a placement of 150 million, in both cases at HK$1.60 per share.
The company said it would expand its retail outlets in China, Australia and New Zealand to 510 shops by April 1998, from the current 349 shops, and over 1,000 outlets after 2000.
It also makes jeans for retailers including The GAP, JC Penney, Phillip Van Heusen, Structure and Haggar.
HSBC Investment bank Asia Ltd is the global coordinater.
